newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index powers to record close.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index powers to record close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks powered ahead on Wednesday as the Hang Seng Index set a closing high at 15,738.81, up 292.03 points or 1.89 percent, on the rises in U.S. bond prices and stocks, brokers said.

The rally came in reaction to Wall Street's overnight surge on comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, which were seen by investors as suggesting Fed policy remained unchanged, brokers said.
The Dow industrials closed at a record 8,061.65, up 1.96 percent, after Greenspan said the Fed would raise interest rates if needed but suggested that might not happen anytime soon.
James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings, said the market was also lifted by the drop in the U.S. long bond yield.
"I think it's more to do with the long bond yield back below 6.50 (percent). It's psychologically very important," he said.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury ended 1-18/32 up on Tuesday, yielding 6.42 percent, the lowest closing yield for the bond since December 5, 1996.
"Buyers had been holding back in the last couple of days ahead of Greenspan's testimony and they came back and bought stocks," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage.
HBSC Holdings, which had been under profit-taking pressure, had a good rally and ended up HK$6.00 at HK$265.00.
Hongkong Telecom added HK$0.45 to HK$20.40 and China Light rose HK$0.90 to HK$45.10.

Property counters were generally higher on hopes that local property prices were bottoming out soon on the back of anticipated steady interest rates, Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas said.
Cheung Kong jumped HK$1.25 to HK$74.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$2.00 to HK$90.25.

But brokers said overall turnover was not very high, which might see the market consolidating in the short term before advancing further. Turnover was HK$16.31 billion versus HK$14.12 billion on Tuesday.
